trust_decision.summary: guarded_getattr decides, for every untrusted attribute access, whether str.format/format_map may be handed out: it must return the SafeFormatter variant (or Unauthorized for a str-subclass class object) instead of the raw method, because the raw method traverses attributes/items of its arguments. At the pinned commit that substitution is only registered for the exact type str in ContainerAssertions, and guarded_getattr keys the assertion table on type(inst), so a str subclass instance and a str-subclass type fall through to raw getattr/aq_acquire.

landing_point.why: It is the only place that names format/format_map and explains the protection (rules dict for str, format -> safe_format); grepping 'format' from the advisory summary lands here and then next door in safe_formatter.py, whereas the actual defect (type-keyed lookup) lives one module away in guarded_getattr.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The C extension is only a performance mirror of ImplPython and may not even be compiled (PURE_PYTHON=1), so fixing ImplPython.guarded_getattr is enough for the reported Python-level string-formatting bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Plain formatting of public data is legitimate and must keep working: '{}'.format(x) / '{0}'.format(obj) on an exact str has to return the SafeFormatter result, not raise. An over-broad fix that denies every format call (or that assumes ContainerAssertions[str] is always a dict, as the C helper does) breaks legitimate formatting, including the project's own allow-all str override used by tests.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second simple type registered through allow_type() with its own rules dict that special-cases an attribute like format but forgets a sibling method or the subclass case.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: allow_type is the public extension point downstream packages use for simple types; the exact-str rules dict in __init__.py already models a format substitution, so a maintainer could copy it for another type and get the keying wrong.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A guard helper (like guarded_hasattr) that performs getattr/hasattr directly instead of delegating to guarded_getattr.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Each builtin replacement in ZopeGuards is hand-written; a new or refactored helper that touches attributes is a natural place to bypass the single choke point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second formatter path (a format-spec/__format__ or a subclass-specific formatter) that walks fields with plain getattr instead of guarded_getattr/guarded_getitem.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SafeFormatter.get_field is the guarded traversal, but the same file already carries both safe_format and safe_format_map variants; adding a third variant that re-implements traversal is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A delegating wrapper whose __getattr__ forwards attribute access to an inner str, so .format escapes the str-typed guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TaintedString already delegates unknown attributes to self._value; a maintainer adding a similar token/wrapper type would inherit the same raw-format exposure without touching guarded_getattr.

O9_family: protection mechanism bypass / information disclosure through unguarded str.format attribute traversal (CWE-693)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools + a C compiler; pyproject builds AccessControl.cAccessControl from src/AccessControl/cAccessControl.c against headers bundled in include/ and src/; needs Acquisition, ExtensionClass, RestrictedPython, BTrees, Persistence, zExceptions and zope.* at runtime
O10_build.project_tests: src/AccessControl/tests/testZopeGuards.py (TestGuardedGetattr plus restricted-compile/eval tests), test_safe_formatter.py, testZopeSecurityPolicy.py, testImplementation.py; run under zope.testrunner or unittest with PURE_PYTHON=0/1

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Special-case format/format_map only where isinstance(inst, str) in ImplPython.guarded_getattr, missing the str-subclass type receiver (X.format), the type-vs-instance split and the C engine that is the default build.
